trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
Going right, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves; going down, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes left.
Going down would leave both cell (6,1) and cell (6,3) needing the line next, and it can't do both; going left, the next 6 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (4,4). So the line goes up.
Going left, the next 6 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (5,4). So the line goes up.
Going right leaves no safe move afterwards; going up would force the two-exit cells to link up into a loop (or put the numbers out of order). So the line goes left.
The line must go down: up is number 8, which comes later.
Going up leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes right.
Number 4 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going left, the next 3 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (1,6). So the line goes up.
Cell (1,6) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes up.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
Going left leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes down.
Number 6 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Cell (5,5) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes down.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
Cell (4,3) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up.
Going up would strand number 7: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up.
Going up would wall in number 9, the last number. So the line goes left.
Going up would leave both cell (1,1) and cell (1,3) needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
